conviction_note: Balanced: Shopify's habit of beating its own revenue guide (Q2 2026 guided high-twenties, printed 34%) and third-party GMV reads (Jefferies) point to a reported-quarter beat of ~2% over a $3.74B bar, but this name sold its last three beats (-6.9, -6.7, -15.6) and moves on the next-quarter guide, where the Q4 consensus of ~$4.74-4.75B (+29% on $3.67B) sits at or above Shopify's habitual first Q4 guide (mid-to-high twenties last year), with card-network and PayPal evidence of an EU-customs drag on cross-border e-commerce; findings sum +0.1, p_up 50 so the scaled number is 0, abs_move 12 because the option market implies 12.6% and the last four prints moved 7-17%.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $3.74B (Fiscal.ai via Stocktwits 2026-10-15 https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/shop-stock-heads-for-4th-green-week-analysts-see-up-to-10-upside-for-shopify-ahead-of-earnings/cZxWF8LRBAi ; Benzinga $3.74B https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SHOP/earnings-forecasts ; Hudson Labs $3,742M https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/shopify-q3-2026-earnings-preview-shop-results-preview), i.e. +31.5% on Q3 2025 revenue of $2,844M (https://www.shopify.com/investors/press-releases/shopify-beats-across-the-board-q3-shows-growth-efficiency-brand-wins), against the company guide of 'low-thirties' revenue growth and 'mid-to-high twenties' gross profit growth, opex 33-34% of revenue (8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001594805/000159480526000046/exhibit991pressreleaseq220.htm). Q3 EPS consensus disagrees by source ($0.33-0.46) so EPS is not used. Q4 2026 revenue consensus $4.74B (Benzinga) / $4,750M (Hudson Labs), ~+29% on Q4 2025 revenue $3.67B (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1594805/000159480526000006/exhibit991pressreleaseq420.htm). Note Hudson Labs mis-states Q3 2025 and Q2 2026 revenue, so its consensus is used only where a second source agrees.
positioning_check: Short interest 20.78M shares as of 2026-10-15 settlement, 2.6 days to cover on ~7.9M average volume (https://massive.com/quote/SHOP), roughly 1.6% of ~1.3B shares: not crowded, no squeeze mechanism. Baseline: 25-delta skew +12.23 vol points (downside paid), ATM IV 140%, event-implied move 12.57%, put/call OI 0.91; run-up -4.5% over 5 days, +0.3% over 20 days, 10.4% below the 52-week high, 68% above the 52-week low. The skew agrees with the negative guidance risk filed below, which is therefore treated as partly priced.

findings.finding: Shopify habitually prints above its own revenue guide (Q2 2026 guided 'high-twenties' on 2026-05-05 and printed +34%, $3.58B vs ~$3.44-3.45B consensus), and consensus for Q3 at $3.74B (+31.5%) sits at the low end of the 'low-thirties' guide; Jefferies' review of third-party data (2026-10-15) says GMV could exceed expectations and Cantor expects a beat on GMV, revenue and operating profit, so a print near $3.80-3.84B (+2% vs bar) is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats alone have been sold: Q3 2025 beat ($2.84B vs $2.76B) and the stock fell 6.9%; Q4 2025 beat and fell 6.7%; Q1 2026 beat ($3.17B vs $3.09B) and fell 15.6% on a slower guide; only Q2 2026 (beat plus guide above street) rose 17.0% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the beat habit is known and the sell-side previews say so, which is why it is sized small; if a larger beat were priced the 20-day run-up would not be flat and the skew would not be +12 vol points toward downside.
findings.independence: Jefferies third-party GMV read and Cantor beat call, Stocktwits 2026-10-15 https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/shop-stock-heads-for-4th-green-week-analysts-see-up-to-10-upside-for-shopify-ahead-of-earnings/cZxWF8LRBAi ; Q2 guide history https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/shopify-shares-slide-q1-loss-165700906.html

findings.finding: The Q4 2026 revenue consensus of $4.74-4.75B (+29% on Q4 2025's $3.67B) is at or above where Shopify's first Q4 guide habitually lands: last year it guided Q4 to 'mid-to-high-twenties' growth (then above a 23% FactSet consensus) and the stock still fell; in May 2026 a 'high-twenties' next-quarter guide took the stock down 15.6%, while in August a 'low-thirties' guide above a ~27% street took it up 17%. A 'high-twenties' Q4 guide would read as at-or-below the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide is the line this stock trades on: 2026-05-05 high-twenties next-quarter guide -15.6%; 2026-08-05 low-thirties guide vs ~27% street +17.0%; 2025-11-04 mid-to-high-twenties Q4 guide (above a 23% consensus) with an operating-income miss -6.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +12.2 vol-point put skew already pays for downside, which this agrees with, so it is sized below a point; if the market were confident of a low-thirties Q4 guide the stock would not have given back 4.5% in the last five sessions into the print.
findings.independence: Q4 consensus from two sources: Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SHOP/earnings-forecasts and Hudson Labs https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/shopify-q3-2026-earnings-preview-shop-results-preview ; Q4 2025 base from 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1594805/000159480526000006/exhibit991pressreleaseq420.htm

findings.finding: Card networks and PayPal, reporting after Shopify last spoke, show a cross-border e-commerce slowdown in Q3 tied to the EU's new €3-per-item customs duty from 2026-07-01: Mastercard cross-border card-not-present ex-travel grew 15% in Q3 2026 vs 20% in Q2 and 21% a year ago, citing the EU customs fee and promotional timing; PayPal branded checkout grew 1% with ~70bp drag from EU de minimis removal; Visa's cross-border e-commerce grew 17%, so the read is mixed and sized small (Shopify international GMV grew 37% in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on cross-border; the stock's reaction has followed the total revenue guide (see the guidance finding).
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy evidence from counterparties dated after the Q2 call, not yet confirmed by Shopify; if the market had transmitted it to SHOP, Q4 consensus would sit below +29% rather than at it.
findings.independence: PayPal Q3 2026 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633917/000163391726000086/pypl3q-26earningsrelease.htm (branded checkout +1%); counter-evidence Visa cross-border e-commerce +17% https://www.fxcintel.com/research/analysis/ct-visa-q4-2026-earnings ; EU duty rule https://vatcalc.com/eu/eu-e3-levy-low-value-e-commerce-import-package-july-2026

findings.finding: US consumer e-commerce held up in Q3: Etsy marketplace GMS grew 8.8% (continuing operations, 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30) and Amazon third-party seller services grew 9% despite Prime Day moving into Q2, which Amazon says cost ~400bp of Q3 growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer reads have not been the line Shopify trades on; its reaction follows its own guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy and small: Shopify grows 3x the market, so demand health is mostly a floor rather than an upside driver; it would show as a higher Q3 bar if fully transmitted, and consensus sits at the low end of the guide.
findings.independence: Amazon Q3 2026 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001018724/000101872426000038/amzn-20260930xex991.htm (third-party seller services +9%, Prime Day shift ~400bp)

findings.finding: Amazon moved Prime Day to 23-26 June 2026 (announced 2026-06-02), pulling the competing-promotion lift Shopify merchants saw in Q3 2025 (Prime Day in July) into Q2 2026; this was public before Shopify's 2026-08-05 Q3 guide, so it lands inside the guided range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, which got the shifted Prime Day, beat its high-twenties guide by ~6 points and rose 17%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it predates the Q3 guide; left in at near zero because Mastercard also cites promotional timing for the Q3 slowdown.
findings.independence: Mastercard cites timing of large retail promotional events, https://www.fxcintel.com/research/analysis/ct-mastercard-q3-2026-earnings (shares a document with the cross-border finding)

findings.finding: Shopify and Meta announced (2026-09-21/22) that Meta's Muse assistant will complete purchases through Shop Pay across Shopify stores, and the Fall '26 Edition (2026-10-28) made agentic checkout default infrastructure; Jefferies said clearer details on the Meta/Muse relationship on the call could support the stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose ~7% the day the Muse deal was announced (2026-09-22); Q2 2026 call stressed agentic commerce and AI-driven orders tripling.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is priced (+7% that day); only a quantified economics or volume disclosure on the call would be new, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Jefferies comment via Stocktwits 2026-10-15 https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/shop-stock-heads-for-4th-green-week-analysts-see-up-to-10-upside-for-shopify-ahead-of-earnings/cZxWF8LRBAi ; Fall '26 Edition https://coalitiontechnologies.com/blog/shopify-editions-fall-26

findings.finding: Shopify is testing and trimming subscription economics in Q4: annual-billed Grow and Advanced were raised to $89 and $359 on 2026-10-15 and reverted on 2026-10-16 (consistent with an A/B test), the Plus 1% sales cashback was removed on 2026-10-02 and Plus lists at $2,300/month; a small support for subscription revenue in the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscription solutions (~22% of revenue, +22% in Q2) has not been the line the stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: A pricing-page diff no aggregator carries, but small relative to merchant solutions; if it mattered the Q4 gross-margin consensus would have moved.

baseline_tension: The evidence is balanced against a +12.2 vol-point put skew and a -4.5% five-day slide: the reported-quarter beat cuts against the skew while the Q4-guide and cross-border risks agree with it, so nothing here says the option market is wrong and p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its last three revenue beats): reported-quarter beat cut from +1.0 to +0.6, p_up from 51 to 50

Lesson 7 / definition (a finding that agrees with a +12 vol-point put skew is probably partly priced): Q4-guide negative cut from -1.0 to -0.8; short interest 1.6% of shares, not crowded, so no squeeze shrink
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): cross-border finding net of Visa's +17% counter cut from -0.4 to -0.3
Lesson 6 (inside what the company already guided): Prime Day shift cut from -0.2 to -0.1
Lesson 6 bar check: Q3 bar sourced to company guide plus three agreeing estimates, Q4 bar to two agreeing estimates, so no cap applied
Lesson 5 (proxies filed small, not dropped): peer and card-network findings left at their draft sizes
